What’s in the export

The zip holds a timestamped transcript-<LANGUAGE>.txt per language, plus, per target language, a pairs-<TARGET>.jsonl (each source line matched to its translation, with a confidence field) and a finetune-<TARGET>.jsonl in OpenAI chat format, ready to upload to a fine-tuning job.

    How schedules work

    Capture starts and stops on its own inside each window of the schedules ticked for it. If it is already running when a window opens, it keeps running and stops at the window’s end. Pressing Stop during a window holds it until the next scheduled start. Starting by hand outside a window is never stopped by a schedule. Windows that overlap or touch run as one session.
    Times follow Relay's time zone, including daylight saving. The machine and the relay must be running for a schedule to fire; a window already under way when the relay starts is picked up, and one missed entirely is skipped.

    Blocklist

    Edited in blocklist.txt with one word or phrase per line. Changes to the file are picked up within about two seconds, no restart. You can also edit it here.

    How matching works

    Matches are removed outright: no asterisks, no gap, nothing on screen to notice. Case and accents are ignored (nino matches niño) and only whole words match, so ass will not touch class.
    Each feed is filtered on its own, so to remove a word everywhere, list it in each language.

A line that never reaches one is committed by the force a line break backstop, always at a word boundary so a word is never cut in half.       Your sound desks, live: channel names, mutes, faders and scenes, the sends into each mix, a
      watchdog for changes nobody made through Relay, and mic names from Planning Center.
      
    
      
    
      
    
      
      
      Mic names from Planning Center
      
      
      The next service's mics, from the Planning Center page's Team and mics tab, give each desk
        channel the name of the person on it. Nothing goes to a desk until you confirm.
      
      
      
      
      
    
      
    
      
      
      Watchdog
      
      
      Save what each desk should look like, then pick who hears when a name, a watched mute or the
        scene changes without Relay doing it. Their phone buzzes until they read it (Crew notifications).
      
      
      
    
      
    
      
      
      I/O patch from a show file
      
      
      The desk does not tell Relay what is patched to its inputs, so export the show (the .tar.gz
        from the desk's USB or Director) and choose it here. Relay lists each input channel's name and socket, and
        what the patched outputs carry, for the signal map. Avantis and dLive only; nothing is written to the desk
        or the file.
      
      
      
    
      
    
      
      
      Desks
      
      
      
      
      
        
        
      
      
      
      Relay talks to each desk over its own control protocol (Allen & Heath MIDI over TCP,
        Behringer OSC, Yamaha RCP). These drivers are built from the published protocols and have not been tried on
        a real desk yet: try them before a service. On macOS and Windows, allow incoming connections the first time
        Relay asks; an X32 or WING answers over UDP.

      Dante 
      
    
      The Dante devices Relay finds on its Dante network: stage boxes, Dante Virtual Soundcard and Dante
      Via. Each appears once by its Dante name, with the transmit channels it announces and whether its control port
      answers. The routing matrix below can change which channel a receive channel listens to; everything else on this
      page only looks. Renaming, gain, sample rate, latency, clock leader and AES67 mode stay in Dante Controller. Works
      with Dante devices.
      

    
      
      
      Devices
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
        
      
          
      NameAddressModelControl portChannels
      
          
        
      
      
      
      
      A device that is alive (it sends its multicast heartbeat) but whose control port is silent is
        shown as such. The heartbeat does not cross a router, so from the main network only the control port tells.
        Between the main network and a Dante VLAN, the router has to
        let UDP through to the control port (4440 for most devices, 24440 for Dante Via).
      
    
      
    
      
      
      Routing
      
      
      Receive channels down, transmit channels across. A dot is a live subscription; click a cell to
        subscribe that receive channel to that transmit channel, or click the dot to clear it. Every change asks
        first, names what it replaces, and can be undone. Changing a subscription is untested on real
        Dante gear: Relay reads the device back after each change and says plainly when it cannot confirm it.
      
      
      
        
        
        
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
        
      
          
          
        
      
      
      
      
      A locked receive channel (the house PA feed, say) is never changed by Relay, not by a
        change here and not by a preset. An administrator locks and unlocks channels with the lock button. A network
        under Dante Domain Manager refuses changes unless Relay has its credentials, which Relay does not support
        yet; the refusal is shown as it comes.
